Mira: fyi getting multiple support tickets about higher tail latency traced to the text-generation runtime canary. p95 jumped starting around 2026-11-05T12:34Z when v2.14.0 canary was promoted to 10% weight.
Kevin: saw the alert in grafana — p95 from ~110ms -> ~430ms, p99 from ~850ms -> ~2.7s in eu-west-1 pools routing to canary.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout v2.14.0 completed (3/3 canary hosts) at 2026-11-05T12:34:12Z
Juan: was that full canary or a low-risk knob? I thought we had 1% for kv/cache changes.
Mira: it was supposed to be 1% but traffic shaping accidentally set 10% for this workload. that caused customer-visible impact.
Samir: quick triage: no JVM GC spikes on sidecars; GPU util steady 50-75%. tail latency appears to line up with long KV cache lookup ms in runtime logs.
Mira: pasted sample logs from canary during spike:

```
[2026-11-05T12:36:07Z] request_id=abc123 model=redwood-7B seq_len=512 kv_lookup_ms=28 kernel_exec_ms=320 total_ms=410
[2026-11-05T12:36:07Z] request_id=abc124 model=redwood-7B seq_len=64  kv_lookup_ms=4  kernel_exec_ms=30  total_ms=72
[2026-11-05T12:36:08Z] request_id=abc125 model=redwood-7B seq_len=1024 kv_lookup_ms=460 kernel_exec_ms=330 total_ms=820
```

Mira: those kv_lookup spikes look bad. v2.14.0 introduced "adaptive KV prefetch" per the changelog.
Kevin: changelog note: "adaptive KV prefetch + fused attention kernel". link: https://internal/release/2.14.0
Samir: hypothesis: prefetch logic triggers blocking IO on misses for long-context patterns, saturating worker threads and delaying kernel launches.
Mira: plan: 1) reduce canary traffic to 0% routing immediately; 2) run isolated perf harness against canary with and without prefetch; 3) bisect commits touching kv cache/prefetch.
Kevin: routing override pushed to set canary weight to 0%.
routing-bot: routing policy updated 12026-11-05T12:48:09Z: canary weight -> 0%
Mira: Kevin, can you run loadtest with synth_longseq profile to reproduce? use qps 40 for 5m.
Kevin: running `./tools/loadtest --target canary --profile synth_longseq.json --qps 40 --duration 5m`
Kevin: baseline run (canary with v2.14.0) shows p95 ~440ms, p99 ~2.6s
Kevin: toggled runtime flag `kv_prefetch=false` in canary config and re-ran loadtest.
Kevin: with prefetch disabled: p95 dropped to ~130ms, p99 ~890ms. looks like prefetch is the regression vector.
Mira: good repro. Is it prefetch algorithm itself or an interaction with the new fused attention kernel? Need to bisect.
Juan: commits to consider: a1b2c3 (adaptive prefetch implementation), d4e5f6 (scheduler inflight tuning), f7g8h9 (attention fusion reorder). prioritize kv prefetch refactor first.
Samir: starting git bisect. marking v2.13.9 as good, v2.14.0 as bad. test harness is `tools/test_perf.sh --synth_longseq` which exits non-zero if p95 > 300ms.

```
git checkout runtime-release
git bisect start v2.14.0 v2.13.9
# test runner will be invoked by perf-bot
```

ops-bot: perf-bot queued perf run for commit b2c9f (kv prefetch refactor)
ops-bot: perf-bot: run completed for b2c9f 12026-11-05T12:58:40Z: p95 385ms (bad)
ops-bot: perf-bot queued perf run for commit e3d1a (scheduler backpressure tweak)
ops-bot: perf-bot: run completed for e3d1a 12026-11-05T13:01:12Z: p95 120ms (good)

Mira: bisect points to the prefetch refactor as the regression. good narrow suspect.
Kevin: minimal repro seems to be long-seq workloads where prefetch issues cause cache miss IO that blocks worker threads.
Juan: pulled flamegraph from a canary host under synth_longseq: main runtime thread shows time in `kv_cache::fetch_async` waiting on `io_wait` with many callers blocked.
Mira: mitigation options: revert prefetch commit / rollback runtime to v2.13.9; add a runtime flag to disable prefetch; throttle concurrent prefetch requests per-request; make prefetch fully async and not hold scheduling locks.
Samir: immediate customer mitigation: rollback canary and notify affected customers. we already set canary weight to 0 but need rollback for safety.
Mira: agree. Juan, open incident and draft customer-facing update. tag support-bot when ready.
Juan: drafting incident note: "We're investigating a latency regression affecting a subset of requests after a canary runtime rollout. Canary routing reduced to 0%, and we've initiated a rollback to v2.13.9. We will provide timeline and RCA when available." :writing_hand:
Samir: I'll add a perf unit test for long-context workloads into CI and gate changes to kv cache behavior behind perf checks.
Kevin: I'll run a 2-hour soak on canary after rollback to confirm p95/p99 stay stable, and coordinate with product before re-enabling any rollout.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback to runtime v2.13.9 started at 2026-11-05T13:02:07Z on canary hosts (3/3)
Kevin: rollback completed. smoke tests show p95 ~125ms, p99 ~870ms 12026-11-05T13:08:15Z — back to baseline.
Mira: follow-ups and owners:
- Samir: open PR with bisect findings, add minimal repro harness + perf test, propose throttle fix for prefetch 1due EOD
- Juan: finalize incident update to customers + write incident timeline doc 1due in 1 hour
- Kevin: run 2-hour soak and report metrics to this thread 1start now
- Mira: schedule postmortem with eng-runtime + eng-platform to decide long-term fix

Mira: rollout/process lessons:
- add perf-gate that covers long-context and KV/cache paths before merging prefetch changes
- stricter canary weights for scheduling/cache changes (<=1%) and staged ramp-up
- runtime flags to hot-toggle risky features per-cluster (already used here)

support-bot: incident-created: #INC-2026-437 (Mira) 12026-11-05T13:08:59Z — customers notified and escalation channel opened
Juan: notified affected customers, they asked if a prod rollback will happen. we should confirm after the soak and decide default rollout plan.
Kevin: soak at 30m shows stable metrics; will update after 2hr mark.
Mira: thanks all. closing the customer escalation for now; will reconvene for postmortem and track the fix PR. :thumbsup:
